120	## 3. R2 — the forced compile break, and the `type_chunk` decision
121	
122	### 3.1 The break
123	
124	`beamr 0.19.x` added a tenth field to `ParsedModule`
125	(`~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-*/beamr-0.19.2/src/loader/load.rs:40`):
126	
127	```rust
128	/// Raw `Type` chunk bytes, carried VERBATIM for re-emission (#95).
129	pub type_chunk: Option<Vec<u8>>,
130	```
131	
132	The workspace has **exactly one** `ParsedModule` struct literal —
133	`crates/aion-awl/src/mir/select/assemble.rs:59-69` — so exactly one E0063.
134	(`crates/aion/tests/awl_bc4_differential/abi.rs:105-109` only *decodes* one;
135	`inspect_analysis.rs`, `inspect_support.rs`, `inspect_expect.rs`, `tests.rs`,
136	`inspect_tests.rs` only take `&ParsedModule`. Adding a field breaks none of
137	them.)
138	
139	### 3.2 The decision: `type_chunk: None`, argued from beamr's source
140	
141	`None` is not a default of convenience here; it is the only truthful value, and
142	beamr 0.19.2's own source says so in three places.
143	
144	1. **`type_chunk` is the raw `Type` chunk of a module that was *decoded*.**
145	   `load.rs:362` — `let type_chunk = find_chunk(&chunks, b"Type").map(<[u8]>::to_vec);`
146	   It is populated only by reading a `Type` chunk out of an input container.
147	   `assemble` has no input container: it *synthesises* a module from AWL MIR
148	   (`assemble.rs:25-73`), and its parts (`builder.rs:209-225`, `BuilderParts` =
149	   `atom_table`, `atoms`, `literals`, `imports`, `lambdas`) contain no type
150	   table and no OTP type information of any kind. There is nothing to carry.
151	
152	2. **The field's only consumer is typed-register re-emission.** The doc comment
153	   at `load.rs:33-39` is explicit: *"Typed-register operands index into this
154	   chunk. beamr's runtime never reads the table, but the encoder must re-emit it
155	   or every emitted typed register dangles."* `encode_module`
156	   (`encode/container.rs:116, 157-159`) uses it for exactly two things: to set
157	   `AtomEncoder::type_chunk_present`, and to append a verbatim `Type` chunk.
158	
159	3. **The AWL selector emits no typed registers, so the field is inert on this
160	   path — and beamr *refuses* rather than degrades if that ever changes.**
161	   `encode/compact.rs:106-133` guards the single operand writer:
162	
163	   ```rust
164	   if !atoms.type_chunk_present {
165	       return Err(EncodeError::TypedRegisterWithoutTypeChunk { .. });
166	   }
167	   ```
168	
169	   with the comment: *"a silent fallback wearing a success exit"* — precisely the
170	   thing it will not do. Measured in this tree: the selector constructs nine
171	   `Operand` variants (`Operand::X` ×76, `Unsigned` ×55, `Label` ×40, `Atom` ×33,
172	   `Y` ×25, `List` ×7, `Literal` ×6, `Integer` ×6) and **zero**
173	   `Operand::TypedRegister`. All three `Operand::TypedRegister` occurrences under
174	   `crates/aion-awl/src/mir/select/` are read-side match arms —
175	   `inspect_support.rs:351`, `:428`, `:442` — as is the one in
176	   `crates/aion/src/runtime/module.rs:224`. There is not one construction site
177	   in the workspace.
178	
179	   So with `type_chunk: None` the guard is unreachable today, and if a future
180	   AWL lowering ever emitted a `#tr{}` operand it would produce a hard
181	   `EncodeError`, not a container that beamr reads and `beam_disasm` cannot —
182	   which is the *safer* of the two states, not the weaker one.
183	
184	4. **A non-`None` value would be a fabrication.** Setting
185	   `type_chunk: Some(vec![])` would flip `type_chunk_present` to `true` and emit
186	   an empty `Type` chunk into every AWL-compiled module, disarming the guard
187	   while promising a table that exists but indexes nothing. `container.rs:126-133`
188	   records that `Type` is one of the chunks measured to be genuinely optional to
189	   `beam_disasm` (OTP 29), so emitting an empty one buys nothing and costs the
190	   refusal.
191	
192	**Ruling: `type_chunk: None` at `assemble.rs:68`, with a comment recording (3) —
193	that the AWL emitter constructs no typed registers, so the field is absent
194	because there is no type table, not because one was dropped.** No `#[allow]`,
195	no blind default anywhere else.
196

## 4. R2 — `type_chunk` decision and validated patch

The decision was made from beamr 0.19.2 source, not from a default guess:

- `loader/load.rs:32-40` defines `type_chunk` as raw, verbatim `Type` bytes whose
  indices are used by typed registers.
- `loader/load.rs:360-362` populates it only with
  `find_chunk(&chunks, b"Type").map(<[u8]>::to_vec)` while decoding an input
  container.
- Aion's assembler synthesises a module from `BuilderParts`; `builder.rs:209-225`
  shows those parts contain atoms, literals, imports, and lambdas, but no type
  table or type information.
- All three `Operand::TypedRegister` occurrences in
  `crates/aion-awl/src/mir/select/` are read-side match arms in
  `inspect_support.rs:351,428,442`; there is no construction site.
- `loader/encode/container.rs:116,157-159` uses `type_chunk.is_some()` to arm the
  operand encoder and conditionally re-emits the bytes. `Some(Vec::new())` would
  falsely claim a table exists and emit an empty `Type` chunk.
- `loader/encode/compact.rs:106-132` returns
  `EncodeError::TypedRegisterWithoutTypeChunk` if a typed register is ever emitted
  without that chunk. That hard failure is the desired future behavior.

Therefore `None` is truthful: there is no type table to carry, not a table that
was dropped.

## 4. R2 — `type_chunk` decision and validated patch

The decision was made from beamr 0.19.2 source, not from a default guess:

- `loader/load.rs:32-40` defines `type_chunk` as raw, verbatim `Type` bytes whose
  indices are used by typed registers.
- `loader/load.rs:360-362` populates it only with
  `find_chunk(&chunks, b"Type").map(<[u8]>::to_vec)` while decoding an input
  container.
- Aion's assembler synthesises a module from `BuilderParts`; `builder.rs:209-225`
  shows those parts contain atoms, literals, imports, and lambdas, but no type
  table or type information.
- All three `Operand::TypedRegister` occurrences in
  `crates/aion-awl/src/mir/select/` are read-side match arms in
  `inspect_support.rs:351,428,442`; there is no construction site.
- `loader/encode/container.rs:116,157-159` uses `type_chunk.is_some()` to arm the
  operand encoder and conditionally re-emits the bytes. `Some(Vec::new())` would
  falsely claim a table exists and emit an empty `Type` chunk.
- `loader/encode/compact.rs:106-132` returns
  `EncodeError::TypedRegisterWithoutTypeChunk` if a typed register is ever emitted
  without that chunk. That hard failure is the desired future behavior.

Therefore `None` is truthful: there is no type table to carry, not a table that
was dropped.

```diff
@@ -66,6 +66,11 @@

+        // If that changes, beamr rejects encoding with
+        // TypedRegisterWithoutTypeChunk rather than writing a dangling index.
+        type_chunk: None,
```
